title: No composition path between ParsedHeader and parse_header_typed; caller must plumb raw bytes manually
description:
The crate's main public surface is `ParsedMessage`/`ParsedHeader`/`ParsedPart`. The new typed API is `parse_header_typed(form, raw_bytes)`. There is no glue function joining them.

header_typed.rs:23-28 module docstring tells the caller:

    "These types are independent of the [`crate::ParsedHeader`] surface, which
     continues to expose only the decoded raw string. Add a typed view on top
     of an existing `ParsedHeader` by slicing the original bytes covered by
     [`crate::ParsedPart::header_range`] and feeding the field value to
     [`parse_header_typed`]."

This sentence offloads three responsibilities onto every caller:

1. Locate `ParsedPart::header_range` for the header they want (it covers the *whole part header block*, not a single field).
2. Slice within that range to find the specific field's value bytes (the caller must parse the header block themselves — defeating the point of using mime-tree).
3. Determine the field boundary (the byte after `:` to the byte before the field's CRLF) — RFC 5322 §2.2 has folding rules the caller must re-implement.

Caller-facing consequence: a caller who wants `header:From:asAddresses` cannot write:

    let typed = parse_header_typed_for(&msg, "From", HeaderForm::Addresses);

They must write a custom header-line locator using `ParsedPart::header_range`, hand-roll field-value extraction, and feed bytes to `parse_header_typed`. The crate's two public APIs do not compose.

A typical convenience constructor would be one of:

    impl ParsedMessage {
        pub fn header_typed(&self, raw: &[u8], name: &str, form: HeaderForm)
            -> Option<HeaderValueTyped>;
    }

    pub fn parse_header_typed_from(raw: &[u8], header: &ParsedHeader, form: HeaderForm)
        -> HeaderValueTyped;

Without these, the user-facing experience is: "the crate gives you a `ParsedHeader` but you still have to do byte-range arithmetic to use the typed parsing it just added".

This is P3 because the workaround (write a header locator) is mechanical and standard for byte-range-indexed parsers. But the module docstring explicitly directing callers to do plumbing themselves is a smell — it documents a missing convenience rather than providing it.

Line refs:
- header_typed.rs:23-28 — module docstring explicitly offloading the composition.
- part.rs — `ParsedHeader` and `ParsedPart::header_range` (not read in this review pass; cited from AGENTS.md public-surface notes).
close_reason: Final API additions: (.14) Added EmailAddress::is_addressable() helper; keeps the Option<String> address field but eliminates the defensive is_some() boilerplate at every call site. Doctest demonstrates the filter pattern. (.28) Added HeaderForm::Text and HeaderValueTyped::Text(String) implementing RFC 8621 §4.1.2.2 — whitespace unfold, RFC 2047 decode (via mail-parser's parse_unstructured), NFC normalisation (via new unicode-normalization dep). parse_text helper, asText accepted by FromStr and emitted by Display. Module-level table now lists all 7 RFC 8621 forms. Tests cover RFC 2047 decode and NFD->NFC normalisation. (.29) Fixed misleading module doc that directed callers at ParsedPart::header_range slicing; the natural path is header.value.as_bytes(). Added parse_header_typed_from(&ParsedHeader, HeaderForm) convenience helper that wraps that pattern.
